## Update and history rules

When an explicit owner-approved decision arrives, inspect the actual source where accessible, record its filename/title, decision date/reference, approval status, service scope, exceptions and supersession evidence. Do not treat a newer proposal as approval. Record inaccessible originals and distinguish owner-reported extracts from inspected documents. Never label source coverage exhaustive without an inventory.

Create a new dated version directory (append a sequence for same-day updates); retain prior versions. Update this pointer, CHANGELOG.md and manifest.json together in the same development-branch commit. Every modified rule must preserve its former source and supersession relationship. Git history also preserves each revision. Do not overwrite an old dated snapshot to disguise a changed policy. A published page must cite its applicable internal rule IDs in its development brief.

Store only sanitised customer-facing facts and development status. No customer records, credentials, supplier costs, salaries, margins, private budgets or management correspondence. Do not depend on static-host dot-directory handling for confidentiality. These files are not linked in website navigation, sitemap or customer templates.

Work only on phase1/customer-journey-repairs and staging. Preserve the approved homepage. No production deployment/settings, final VIP terms/FAQs, subscription activation, unverified uploads or automatic customer messages. Stop for owner review before publishing customer-facing policy changes.
